Name: issue-fo.vm
Description: Exports the issues into a PDF that visually reminds of JIRA's default styling. It includes all field values, time tracking, issue links, attachments, image thumbnails, comments, worklogs and change history. It also enables embedding the issue attachments within the PDF document, to distribute your issues together with their file attachments, as a single self-containing package. Or, use this as a great starting point for customization (like hiding fields) or for developing totally new templates.

Name: issue-navigator-fo.vm
Description: Landscape-oriented issue list template. It uses the filter's own column layout: when you show, hide or move columns around in JIRA, those will appear, disappear or move also in your PDFs. Check the template code if you need dynamically configurable fields in your exports.

Name: reference-manual-fo.vm
Description: Wird möglicherweise noch verwendet. Expressions Reference Manual is the complete reference of the expressions to be used in the PDF templates. Use this both as a cheatsheet (just copy the references to your template!) and as a live test environment (modify and export this template).

Name: release-notes-fo.vm
Description: Release Notes document template, with customizable content and branding. Advantages over the default Release Notes generated by JIRA: you can precisely specify what fields to include, you can include additional content like installation instructions and pricing information, you can use company branding (logos, colors), etc. This is an easy and powerful way to get your complete software version documentation out of JIRA.

Name: requirements-specification-fo.vm
Description: Template to export JIRA issues into SRS documents (Software Requirement Specification), based on IEEE standard 830-1998. Enables fast external validation of a set of requirements, easy distribution of requirement baselines, or generating your final SRS documents. Even if it may not fully meet the needs of your SRS style, it's a great starting point for customization. (It features a book-like Table of Contents and PDF bookmarks, too.) It uses requirements-specification.groovy.

Name: requirements-specification.groovy
Description: Used by requirements-specification-fo.vm.

Name: sales-report-fo.vm
Description: General report template that also exports custom charts generated from JIRA data to PDF documents. Although the default reporting domain is sales data, it can be totally reconfigured to calculate and display any type of Performance Metrics. It uses sales-report.groovy and charts.groovy.

Name: sales-report.groovy
Description: Used by sales-report-fo.vm.

Name: service-desk-tool.groovy
Description: JIRA Service Desk tool used by the templates that connect to JIRA Service Desk to download ticket data.

Name: story-card-fo.vm
Description: Template to export physical story cards from JIRA issues, for Scrum and Kanban teams. It can be used with or without JIRA Agile (previously known as GreenHopper).

Name: tempo-tool.groovy
Description: Tempo tool used by the templates that connect to Tempo to download worklog data.

Name: timesheet-fo.vm
Description: Exports timesheets and time-based invoices from JIRA or Tempo worklogs. It calculates time and amount (money) subtotals and grand totals for the whole issue list. It can optionally filter non-billable worklogs, and get customer information from Tempo. If you run time and material based projects, turn JIRA into a powerful invoicing system with this template.

Name: traceability-matrix-fo.vm
Description: Renders a 2D matrix with two sets of issues, and uses the cells to visualize relations (ex: directed dependencies) between the issues. Traceability matrixes are used to match parts of high-level design, detailed design, test plan, and test cases in Requirements Management and Test Management. It uses traceability-matrix.groovy.
